name: fast-space-clicks-do-not-blink
description:
pressing several space dots in quick succession made the whole window blink, sidebar and web card together.

A dot press is swipe.jumpTo. When a press landed while an earlier glide was still settling, createSwipeMachine.jumpTo rebased spaceIndex onto the settle it was abandoning. Two things read that rebase. The controller's frame loop announces a change of spaceIndex as an arrival, so the browser got a full sidebarSpaceSelected for a space the rail was only passing through - tabs swapped, the backdrop tint restarted its crossfade, the sidebar snapshot was rebuilt. And displayP is measured from spaceIndex, so leaving it behind teleported the rail a whole pane in one frame. Driven headlessly, the five presses below produced five announcements and four teleports (build/scripts/swipe-controller-test.mjs).

The run is in three parts. The first two presses are unhurried and are the CONTROL: one moves to Third and one comes back to Elsewhere, each gated on a run-log line, so nothing after them can pass on presses that landed on the sidebar background. The Third capture in between is what proves the graded region can move at all.

Then the burst: Editing, Third, Editing, Third, and home to Elsewhere, as fast as the harness sends them - a 100ms sleep plus two cgevent spawns per press, so the real spacing is longer than 100ms and is not measured here. The last press names the space the run is already in, so a coalesced burst has nothing for the browser to do and the card holds the same white favicon-page.html on both sides of it. Editing and Third both render on cream, so a switch that painted is plainly visible in a region carrying no text.

Why the burst is not fired under a capture, which would give a frame per press: measured on 2026-08-30, a press sent while a rapidcap stream is live moves the pointer and lands its hover on the dot and produces no DOM click at all, while the same press outside a capture works. Keys are unaffected, which is why key_during_capture does not have this problem. The run-log count below is what carries the claim instead, and it is the stronger half anyway - a switch the user never asked for is visible there whether or not a frame caught it.

What is NOT claimed: nothing here says a burst is fast, or that the rail takes the shortest path between two presses. It says the browser is asked to switch only for the press the rail comes to rest on.

actions.note: GATE: Elsewhere's own tab has committed, so the card holds the white page the assertions read
let the rail draw and the dots bar take its place at the foot of the sidebar
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

actions.expression: [...document.querySelectorAll('.spacedots .sdot')].map((d) => { const r = d.getBoundingClientRect(); return (d.dataset.spaceIndex ?? 'ov') + '@' + Math.round(r.left + r.width / 2) + ':' + Math.round(r.top + r.height / 2); }).join(' ')
actions.note: which dot is which space, and where. The presses below are fixed screen points, so this is the record of what they were aimed at.
the pointer travels to the dot before it presses, as a hand does
CONTROL 1: one unhurried press on Third's dot
Third's tab is cold at launch, so this commits only if the press reached the dot
Third's cream page, the other half of the sensitivity control below
CONTROL 2: back to Elsewhere, so the burst starts and ends in the same space
the card before the burst - Elsewhere's white page

Editing, Third, Editing, Third, and home to Elsewhere. The last press decides, and it names the space the burst started in. interval_ms is the SLEEP between presses, not the gap: two cgevent processes are spawned per press on top of it, so the real spacing is longer and unmeasured. What the burst has to beat is the settle spring, which runs settleDur (0.28s) stretched up to 2.2x for a multi-pane jump - a press landing inside that is an interruption rather than a fresh gesture, and the run-log count below is what says whether it was.
past the settle spring and past ShowTab's 250ms damage-heal reattach
where the rail came to rest, read off the machine rather than off a picture

assertions.desc: CALIBRATION: five dots, three of them spaces, on the row the presses target. The window content starts at 0,30 on this VM, so these page points are the screen points the actions send. A layout change has to fail here rather than send the burst into the sidebar background. Overview and + sit in a flex row of their own around the dots' scroller, which rounds their position independently and shifts each by 2px - the three room dots the burst actually presses did not move.

The rail is parked on pane 2, Elsewhere, with nothing in flight and nothing unacknowledged. This is the burst's last press landing, read off the machine - it is what makes the two stability assertions below the right question rather than a picture of a surface that never moved.

assertions.label: control-1-a-single-press-switches-space
assertions.desc: CONTROL: one unhurried press on a dot reaches SelectSpace. Without it the absence below could be satisfied by presses that landed on nothing.

assertions.label: control-2-and-the-run-is-back-where-it-started
assertions.desc: CONTROL: the burst begins in Elsewhere, which is what makes the stability assertions below the right question to ask.

assertions.label: the-burst-never-switched-to-a-space-it-passed-through
assertions.desc: Editing is reachable in this run ONLY through the burst - the two control presses name Third and Elsewhere. A press the rail never came to rest on must not switch the browser.

assertions.label: the-burst-asks-for-at-most-one-switch
assertions.desc: Two control presses plus five burst presses ask the browser to switch three times at the very most. Each switch swaps the card's tab, restarts the tint crossfade and rebuilds the sidebar snapshot, so the count IS the blinking.

The web card is unchanged across the burst, because the last press names the space it started in. Under the old build the burst left the window on whichever space its spurious announcements last reached.
assertions.note: Measured inside the content card, which runs x 205..1015 and y 32..698 on this VM's 1024x768 screen, and to the right of the screen-recording consent panel the capture tool raises at x 380..645. Deliberately clear of peek-target.html's ticking counter, which moves on its own.

assertions.desc: THE SENSITIVITY CONTROL: the same region DOES move when a space switch paints - Third's cream against Elsewhere's white, measured at delta 44.6. Without it the stability assertion above would pass on a blank card, or on a region that can never change.
